source: Grok Bot cursor-github MCP (GetDynamicTools namespace cursor-github), captured 2026-10-30 12:37 CET
read_write_rule: get_*/list_*/search_*/compare_commits are reads; everything else writes

tools.name: add_comment_to_pending_review
description: Add an inline comment to the caller's pending (unsubmitted) review on a pull request, via GraphQL addPullRequestReviewThread. Start the review with create_pull_request_review and no `event`, add
comments one at a time here, then submit_pending_pull_request_review. The reply is the new review thread with its first comment.

review_id.description: The pending review's id (from create_pull_request_review). Looked up when omitted: the caller's one PENDING review on the pull request.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root.

subject_type.description: LINE (default; needs `line`) or FILE for a whole-file comment.

line.description: Line in the diff the comment applies to (the last line of a range).

tools.name: add_discussion_comment
tools.description: Comment on a discussion (GraphQL `addDiscussionComment`): a new top-level comment, or a reply when `reply_to_id` names a top-level comment (Discussions nest one level; replying to a reply is refused).

reply_to_id.description: Node id of the top-level comment to reply to.

tools.name: add_issue_comment
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments: comment on an issue or on a pull request's conversation (pass the PR number).

tools.name: add_sub_issue
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues: make an existing issue a sub-issue of `issue_number`. An issue has one parent: pass `replace_parent: true` to move it from another.

sub_issue_id.description: The sub-issue's `id` (the numeric id on the issue object, not its number).

tools.name: compare_commits
description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}: how `head` differs from `base` (`status`, `ahead_by`, `behind_by`), one page of the commits between them, and the files changed with their patches.
Pass `base` and `head` as separate arguments, not GitHub REST's single `basehead` path parameter. Both are branches, tags, or SHAs; `head` may be `owner:branch` for a fork.

base.description: Base branch, tag, or commit SHA.

head.description: Head branch, tag, or commit SHA.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: create_branch
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs: create a branch at `sha`, at the head of `from_branch`, or at the head of the default branch. GitHub answers 422 when the branch already exists.

from_branch.description: Branch to start from (default branch when omitted).

sha.description: Exact commit to start from; overrides from_branch.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues: open an issue.

tools.name: create_label
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels: create a label. GitHub answers 422 `already_exists` when the name is taken.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls: open a pull request from an existing branch. `head` is the branch with the changes (`user:branch` for a fork), `base` the target branch.

tools.name: create_pull_request_review
description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews: approve, request changes, or comment, optionally with inline comments on specific files and lines (each needs `path` and `line`, or a legacy
`position`). Omit `event` to leave the review PENDING (unsubmitted): then add comments with add_comment_to_pending_review and publish it with submit_pending_pull_request_review.

event.description: Submit as this; omitted = create a pending review.

body.description: Review summary; required for REQUEST_CHANGES and COMMENT.

commit_id.description: Head SHA the review applies to; defaults to the current head.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root.

line.description: Line in the diff the comment applies to (the last line of a range).

tools.name: delete_discussion_comment
tools.description: Delete a discussion comment (GraphQL `deleteDiscussionComment`). Irreversible; confirm with the user when not explicitly asked.

comment_id.description: The comment's node id (`id`, e.g. DC_kwDO...), from get_discussion_comments.

tools.name: delete_label
description: DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}: delete a label from the repository, removing it from every issue and pull request that carries it. Irreversible; confirm with the user when not explicitly
asked. Always call `list_labels` first.

tools.name: delete_pending_pull_request_review
tools.description: DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}: discard the caller's pending review and every comment queued on it. Only a PENDING review can be deleted; submitted reviews stay.

review_id.description: The pending review's id (from create_pull_request_review). Looked up when omitted: the caller's one PENDING review on the pull request.

tools.name: get_branch
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}: one branch with its head commit and protection summary.

tools.name: get_commit
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}: one commit with its stats and the files it touched (each with a `patch`), by SHA, branch, or tag.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch name, or tag name.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: get_commit_combined_status
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/status: the combined commit status (legacy status API) for a ref, e.g. a pull request's head SHA.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch name, or tag name.

tools.name: get_discussion
tools.description: One discussion by number (GraphQL `repository.discussion`): title, body, category, labels, the accepted answer if any, and counts.

tools.name: get_discussion_comments
tools.description: One page of a discussion's top-level comments (GraphQL `discussion.comments`), each with `isAnswer`; `include_replies` nests up to 100 replies under each (Discussions nest one level).

tools.name: get_file_contents
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} with the raw media type: the file's bytes as text (not the base64 JSON envelope). For a directory GitHub answers with the JSON listing instead.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (default branch when omitted).

tools.name: get_git_tree
description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree_sha}: a tree object. `tree_sha` may be a branch or tag name, or a commit or tree SHA; pass `recursive: true` to list the whole subtree in one call (GitHub
truncates very large trees and says so with `truncated: true`).

tree_sha.description: Tree SHA, commit SHA, branch, or tag.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}: the issue object.

tools.name: get_issue_comment
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{comment_id}: one issue or pull request conversation comment by id (a comment's `id`).

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}: one job of a workflow run with its steps (status, conclusion, timings) and runner details.

tools.name: get_job_logs
description: Plain-text GitHub Actions logs. Provide `job_id` (preferred) for GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs, or `run_id` to get the logs of that workflow run's failed jobs (conclusion
failure or timed_out, latest attempt, at most 3), each under a header naming the job; a run with no failed jobs answers its job list instead. Whole logs past ~50 MiB cannot be fetched; pass
`tail_bytes` to get only the end of each log, where a failure usually is (with `run_id` it defaults to the last 64 KiB per job). Expired logs answer 410.

job_id.description: Job id from list_workflow_run_jobs. Give this or run_id, not both.

run_id.description: Workflow run id; returns the logs of the run's failed jobs.

tail_bytes.description: Return only the last N bytes of each log.

tools.name: get_label
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}: one label. Always call `list_labels` first.

tools.name: get_latest_release
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest: the most recent non-prerelease, non-draft release. Always call `list_releases` first.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: GET /user for every GitHub account connected to this Cursor account, as a JSON array of GitHub user objects. Repository tools act as whichever of these can see the repository.

tools.name: get_pull_request
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}: the pull request object (body, head/base, mergeability, change counts).

tools.name: get_pull_request_diff
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number} with the diff media type: the pull request's unified diff as text. GitHub answers 406 when the diff is too large to render; list the files instead.

tools.name: get_release_by_tag
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/tags/{tag}: the release published for a tag. Always call `list_releases` first.

tools.name: get_repository
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}: the repository object.

tools.name: get_tag
description: One tag by name: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/tags/{tag}, and when it is an annotated tag, GET /git/tags/{sha} for the tag object (tagger, message, and the commit it points at). The reply is
`{ref, tag}`; `tag` is null for a lightweight tag, whose `ref.object` is the commit itself.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}: one workflow object (id, name, path, state, badge URL).

workflow_id.description: Numeric workflow id or the workflow file name, e.g. ci.yml.

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}: the workflow run object.

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches: one page of branches.

protected.description: Only protected (true) or only unprotected (false) branches.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_check_runs_for_ref
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs: one page of check runs (GitHub Actions and other Checks API apps) for a ref.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch name, or tag name.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_commits
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits: one page of commits, optionally from a branch or SHA, touching a path, or by author or date range.

sha.description: Branch name or commit SHA to start from (default branch when omitted).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_discussion_categories
tools.description: A repository's discussion categories (GraphQL `repository.discussionCategories`), each with its `id` for list_discussions and whether it is answerable (Q&A).

tools.name: list_discussions
tools.description: One page of a repository's discussions (GraphQL `repository.discussions`), optionally within one category (`category_id` from list_discussion_categories) and ordered by creation or last update.

tools.name: list_issue_comments
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments: one page of an issue's comments.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues: one page of issues. GitHub includes pull requests here (they carry a `pull_request` key).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels: one page of the repository's labels. Pass `issue_number` for GET .../issues/{issue_number}/labels, the labels on one issue or pull request.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_my_repositories
description: GET /user/repos for every GitHub account connected to this Cursor account: one page of the repositories each account can access, as a JSON array holding one array of repository objects per account (in
get_me order). Use it to find a repository's owner/name before calling a repository tool.

affiliation.description: Comma-separated owner, collaborator, organization_member (GitHub's default is all three).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_request_comments
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pull_number}/comments: one page of the pull request's conversation comments (not review comments).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_request_commits
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/commits: one page of the pull request's commits, oldest first (GitHub returns at most 250).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_request_files
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/files: one page of the files a pull request changes, each with its patch.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_request_review_comments
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments: one page of inline review comments (each with path, line, and diff hunk).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_request_reviews
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews: one page of reviews (state APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED, ...).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls: one page of pull requests.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases: one page of releases (drafts and prereleases included), newest first, each with its assets.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_repository_collaborators
description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators: one page of the users with access to the repository, each with its `permissions` and `role_name`. Organization members with access through teams count unless
`affiliation` narrows it.

permission.description: Only collaborators with at least this permission.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_sub_issues
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues: one page of an issue's sub-issues, in priority order.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags: one page of tags, newest first, each with the commit it points at.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_workflow_run_jobs
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs: one page of the run's jobs with their steps (status, conclusion, timings).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_workflow_runs
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs, or /actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs when `workflow_id` is given: one page of workflow runs, newest first, with GitHub's run filters.

workflow_id.description: Workflow id or file name (ci.yml); all workflows when omitted.

actor.description: Login of the user who triggered the run.

created.description: Date range in GitHub search syntax, e.g. >=2026-01-01.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows: one page of the repository's workflows (id, name, path, state).

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: mark_discussion_comment_as_answer
tools.description: Mark (`answer: true`) or unmark a comment as the accepted answer of a Q&A discussion (GraphQL `markDiscussionCommentAsAnswer` / `unmarkDiscussionCommentAsAnswer`).

comment_id.description: The comment's node id (`id`, e.g. DC_kwDO...), from get_discussion_comments.

tools.name: merge_pull_request
description: PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge. Irreversible: check the pull request's mergeable state and its checks first, and confirm with the user when the merge was not explicitly requested.
GitHub answers 405 when the PR is not mergeable and 409 when the head SHA does not match.

sha.description: Head SHA the merge must apply to; refused if the head moved.

tools.name: remove_sub_issue
tools.description: DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issue: detach a sub-issue from its parent (the issue itself is kept).

sub_issue_id.description: The sub-issue's `id` (the numeric id on the issue object, not its number).

tools.name: reply_to_pull_request_review_comment
tools.description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies: reply in an existing review-comment thread.

tools.name: reprioritize_sub_issue
tools.description: PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues/priority: move a sub-issue within its parent's list, placing it after `after_id` or before `before_id` (pass exactly one).

sub_issue_id.description: The sub-issue's `id` (the numeric id on the issue object, not its number).

tools.name: search_code
description: GET /search/code across the repositories every connected account can see, GitHub code-search syntax (e.g. "repo:owner/name path:src language:ts <terms>"). To search inside one repository, put
`repo:owner/name` in `q`. GitHub indexes only the default branch. Results merge across accounts.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: search_commits
tools.description: GET /search/commits with GitHub commit-search syntax (e.g. "repo:owner/name fix login author:octocat"). Runs as every connected account and merges the envelopes (items verbatim, deduplicated).

description:
GitHub search query syntax. A query can mix two kinds of terms:
- Qualifiers such as `repo:owner/name`, `is:open`, `label:bug`, `author:octocat`, separated by spaces. Every qualifier must match:

`author:octocat repo:owner/name` means items by `octocat` in `owner/name`. Exclude with `-`, e.g. `-label:wontfix`. AND / OR / NOT never apply to qualifiers; for `repo:a/b OR repo:c/d`, run one search

per repo.
- Plain text terms, which may be joined with AND / OR / NOT (at most five per query), e.g. `repo:owner/name crash OR panic`.

sort.description: Sort field; best match when omitted.

per_page.description: Results per page (GitHub's default is 30, max 100).

tools.name: search_issues
description: GET /search/issues restricted to issues (`is:issue` is added to the query), e.g. "repo:owner/name is:open label:bug". Runs as every connected account and merges the envelopes (items verbatim,
deduplicated).

description: GET /search/repositories with GitHub repository-search syntax (e.g. "user:octocat language:ts", "org:acme topic:cli"). Runs as every connected account and merges the envelopes (items verbatim,

verbatim, deduplicated).

tools.name: set_pull_request_draft
description: Mark a pull request ready for review (`draft: false`) or convert it back to a draft (`draft: true`). GitHub exposes this only through GraphQL (markPullRequestReadyForReview /
convertPullRequestToDraft), so the reply is that mutation's `pullRequest` object, not the REST one. A pull request already in the requested state is returned as is.

draft.description: true = convert to draft; false = ready.

tools.name: submit_pending_pull_request_review
description: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}/events: submit the caller's pending review as APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, or COMMENT, publishing every comment added to it. `body` is
the review summary (required by GitHub for REQUEST_CHANGES and COMMENT when the pending review has no body).

review_id.description: The pending review's id (from create_pull_request_review). Looked up when omitted: the caller's one PENDING review on the pull request.

tools.name: update_discussion_comment
tools.description: Edit a discussion comment's body (GraphQL `updateDiscussionComment`).

comment_id.description: The comment's node id (`id`, e.g. DC_kwDO...), from get_discussion_comments.

tools.name: update_issue
tools.description: PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}: edit title, body, labels, assignees, or state (with `state_reason`). `labels` and `assignees` replace the existing sets.

tools.name: update_label
tools.description: PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}: rename (`new_name`), recolor, or redescribe a label; issues carrying it follow. Always call `list_labels` first.

color.description: Six-digit hex color without the leading #, e.g. f29513.

tools.name: update_pull_request
tools.description: PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}: change title, body, base branch, or state (open/closed).

tools.name: update_pull_request_branch
tools.description: PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/update-branch: bring the head branch up to date with its base (GitHub's "Update branch"). Asynchronous on GitHub's side (202).

expected_head_sha.description: Refuse if the head has moved past this SHA.

format_note: Long description strings are stored as arrays of chunks (no line over 400 chars); join each array with '' to get the exact reference text. The canonical unchunked copy is /workspace/swarm/specs/grokbot-github-mcp-schemas.json.
